Take the current branch from "in flight" to "merged" in one command: the last step of the dev workflow. It picks up where `/<caller>:sync` and `/<caller>:ready` left off, runs `/<caller>:sync` itself when the branch has no pull request yet, and runs `/<caller>:ready loop` first when ready has never run on the branch. It waits for CI on the exact commit that lands, merges it, deletes the remote branch, and runs `/<caller>:sync remote` so the issue moves to done and linked errors resolve. Every vendor-specific action goes through the repo's configured integrations (`/<caller>:configure`): the source-control host merges a single branch, and a stacking tool, when there is one, lands a whole stack.

**Arguments**, in any order:

- `stack` lands every branch from the base up to and including this one; `branch` (or `no-stack`) lands only this one. Neither: when branches sit below this one in its stack, ask; otherwise only this one lands. Branches above this one are never touched.
- `squash`, `merge` (or `no-squash`), or `rebase` picks the merge method for a single branch. Neither: `squash`, or `merge` when the branch is part of a stack of more than one, so each stacked pull request keeps its own boundary in the base's history. A stack lands by the stacking tool's or the host's own method, so a method passed with `stack` isn't used: say so in the report.
- `no-ready` skips the `/<caller>:ready loop` finish runs on a branch ready never saw (`finish.runReady: false` skips it every time).

## Invariants

- **Invoking this command is the authorization to merge.** Don't ask for a second confirmation. The one question it asks is how much of a stack to land, and only when nothing said.
- **Act through the integrations' ops.** Pull requests, checks, merges, and stacks are reached only through the ops `configure.ts integrations` returns, run as given. Plain `git` is fine for everything local.
- **Never bypass the host:** no admin merge, no auto-merge, no skipping a required check or review, no rerunning someone's CI to get past it.
- **Nothing is pushed between the CI pass and the merge.** The merge is pinned to the commit CI passed on; a head that moved since stops it.
- **Clean up only after the host says merged.** No branch deletion, issue update, or error resolution for a pull request that isn't merged.
- **Run the repo's hooks around this command.** Skip this when the mode is `help`, or when another of these commands is running this one (it runs its own). Once the mode is known, before the first step's work: `node "$DEV_FLOWS_BASE/src/commands/hooks.ts" run before --flow finish --mode <mode>`. When the command ends, finished or stopped, just before its report or before telling the user why it stopped: `node "$DEV_FLOWS_BASE/src/commands/hooks.ts" run finish.after after --flow finish --mode <mode> --branch <branch> --pr <N> --prs '<the numbers of every pull request it lands, bottom first, space-separated>' [--merged --merge-commit <landed>] --outcome <success, when it did its job, else failure>`, leaving out a flag whose value isn't known yet. Pass `--merged` whenever the host said <N> merged, even when what came after (the close-out, the deploy watch) failed, with `--merge-commit` the merge commit the run step read; leave both out when nothing merged. It prints JSON with a `status`. `done`: carry on; `failures`, if any, are hooks that failed at a point that reports them rather than stops, so name them in the report. `agent`: a hook handed you `agent.task` (a prompt from the config, or what a check printed when it exited 2). Do it now, under this command's own rules (the same bar as any fix, and nothing they forbid), then run the same command again with `--after <agent.resume>` for the rest (with `agent.recheck`, that first runs the hook's check again, and it fails like any check when the task didn't satisfy it); a task you can't do with confidence is a stop: say so, and ask. With `agent.recheck` `report`, the task is a list of findings: fix each one you can with confidence and leave the rest, which is not a stop; the check runs again, and what it still finds comes back in `open` rather than as a failure. `open`, in any call's output, lists those findings by hook (`name`, `output`): keep each for the report, where it's listed as open under its hook's name. `stop`: a hook failed (after its fix, when it has one): stop this command and show the user `stop.name` and `stop.output` (the full log is at `stop.log`). `running`: a hook was still running when `--max-wait` ran out, and goes on running: run the same command again with `--wait <running.resume>` in place of any `--after`, until the status is another one, relaying `running.name` and how long it has run. When the host limits how long one command runs, add `--max-wait <a bit under that limit, in seconds>` to every `hooks.ts run`. An exit of 2 means bad arguments or an invalid config: relay its message and stop. At the end, a `stop` can't happen: report the `failures`. When `ran` lists any hook, say in the report which ran at each point, what any task for you changed, what failed, and every finding a hook's `open` left, as open; when no point ran one, leave hooks out of the report.

### 1b. Gates

With `<requireClean>` true, run gate 2 first: the sync below would commit uncommitted changes, and whether they ship is the user's call.

1. **No pull request?** Say `No pull request for <branch>. Running /<caller>:sync to open one...` and run the sync flow (read `$DEV_FLOWS_BASE/flows/claude/sync/flow.md` and follow it, with the same caller, so its commands are `/<caller>:<name>` too) with no arguments: it commits what's uncommitted, pushes, and opens the pull request and its issue. Then run `currentPr` again; still none: stop, `Sync finished but there's still no pull request. Check its output, then re-run /<caller>:finish.` Note that sync ran, so the run phase doesn't run it again, and skip gate 2 (sync committed everything).
2. **Uncommitted changes?** `git status --porcelain` prints anything: stop, `<branch> has uncommitted changes. Commit them (or run /<caller>:sync), then re-run /<caller>:finish.` Don't commit them here: whether they ship is the user's call.
3. **Already merged or closed?** Merged: stop, `Pull request <N> is already merged.` (a `/<caller>:sync remote` closes out its issue). Closed: stop, `Pull request <N> is closed. Reopen it to merge it.`
4. **Targets the base?** The pull request's base branch must be `<base>`, or, with a stacking entry, the branch's parent in its stack (its `parent` op; 1c checks that parent further). Anything else: stop, `Pull request <N> targets <its base>, not <base>. Retarget it to <base>, then re-run /<caller>:finish.` A pull request opened by hand often targets the host's default branch, and landing it there can deploy what the base exists to hold back.

Keep the pull request's number `<N>`, URL, title, draft state, and base branch.

### 1c. Stack and method

**Parent:** With a stacking entry, its `parent` op. When that succeeds and names a branch other than `<base>`, check it hasn't already merged: the source-control entry's `branchPr` op for it (with no source-control entry, skip the check). Merged means it landed, so `<parent>` is the base that pull request merged into, and `<landed>` is the old parent: `/<caller>:sync` moves the branch off it (until then, the branch still holds the landed parent's commits, so compare its own work against `<landed>`, not `<parent>`). Otherwise `<parent>` is the branch the op named. When there's no stacking entry, or its `parent` op fails (the branch isn't tracked): the pull request's base branch when there's a pull request, else `<base>`. With a `<landed>`, stop: `<branch> still sits on <landed>, which already merged. Run /<caller>:sync to move it onto <parent>, then re-run /<caller>:finish.` Merging now would land it into a branch that's already gone.

With a stacking entry, run its `downstack` op: `chain`, `above`, and `size`. Without one, the chain is `[<branch>]`, with `above` 0 and `size` 1.

**Scope:** `stack` or `branch` from the arguments. Neither, and the chain has more than one branch: show the chain bottom first, one line per branch (`#<number> <title>`, `(draft)` for a draft, the current branch marked; each branch's pull request from the `branchPr` op), then ask: `<branch> sits on <chain length - 1> other stacked branch(es). Land the whole chain, or just this branch?`, with the options `Land the whole chain` (every pull request in it merges bottom first) and `Just this branch` (only #<N> merges, into its base <the pull request's base>; the branches below stay open). Otherwise `branch`. `stack` with a chain of one is `branch`. `stack` with no stacking entry: stop, `Landing a stack needs a stacking integration. Run /<caller>:configure stacking, or merge each pull request on its own.`

**Method**, for `branch`: the argument (`no-squash` is `merge`), else `merge` when `size` is more than 1, else `squash`. Keep why (`explicit`, `auto: stack of <size>`, or `auto: single branch`).

### 1d. Chain gates

Only for `stack`, in order:

1. **Every branch has a pull request?** The `branchPr` op for each branch in the chain. Any without one: stop, `Can't land the chain: <branches> have no pull request. Run /<caller>:sync on each, then re-run /<caller>:finish stack.`
2. **Every one still open?** One merged or closed means the stack's record is out of date: stop, `The stack is stale: <branch>'s pull request is <state>. Restack it (/<caller>:sync), then re-run /<caller>:finish.`
3. **Any already failing?** `git fetch origin <every branch in the chain>`, then for each branch the `checks` op on `git rev-parse origin/<branch>`. Any `fail` or `cancelled`: stop, naming the branch and its pull request URL, `Can't land the chain: #<number> has failing checks. Fix it with /<caller>:ready, then re-run /<caller>:finish stack.` A chain that stops halfway leaves part of it merged, so this is checked before anything is written.

Drafts are fine: the merge step marks them ready.

### 1f. Ready

Whether the run phase runs `/<caller>:ready loop` before the CI wait, and why. Not with the `no-ready` argument, nor with `<runReady>` false, nor with `<syncMode>` `remote` (ready pushes, and finish.sync remote means nothing in finish does). Otherwise `node "$DEV_FLOWS_BASE/src/commands/ready.ts" last` prints whether ready has run on this branch: `ran` true means it has (keep its `mode` and short `sha` for the report), so finish doesn't run it; `ran` false means ready never saw this branch, so the run phase runs it. Keep the decision as `<readyRun>`, with its reason (`no-ready`, `finish.runReady`, `finish.sync remote`, `already ran`, or `never ran`).
